alternatives.name: SIM7000
alternatives.note: Full driver: delivery receipts, whitelist/SMS command helpers, network time, operator name.

description: SIMCom SIM7000 modem, lean API: SMS send/receive, HTTP POST over GPRS, USSD, and self-recovery via maintain()

http_post.description: POST a form body over GPRS; up to 3 attempts on failure or 5xx; returns the HTTP status or -1

maintain.description: Call periodically: recovers a silent or off-network modem; returns true when registered

next_sms.description: Read the oldest received SMS (then deleted from the SIM); false if none

ready.description: true if the modem answers AT

registered.description: true when registered on the home or a roaming network

send_sms.description: Send an SMS (max 160 chars); retries twice only if refused before sending

set_pwrkey.description: GPIO driving PWRKEY and its polarity; enables power-cycling in maintain()

sms_from.description: Sender of the SMS read by next_sms()

sms_text.description: Text of the SMS read by next_sms()

ussd.description: Send a USSD code (e.g. *125#) and return the reply text, "" on failure

name: SIM7000Lite

specs.uart: 115200 baud default, 3.3V logic on most boards
specs.voltage: 3.0V - 4.3V (Li-ion); peaks up to 2 A during GSM transmit

tips: Call maintain() every 30-60 s: it soft-resets a modem that stops answering or stays off the network for 3 minutes, and power-cycles it through PWRKEY if set_pwrkey() was called.
send_sms() retries only when the modem refused before sending, so a message is never sent twice.
Incoming SMS: loop on next_sms() and act on sms_from()/sms_text() in your program; each message is deleted from the SIM once read.
Call set_apn() with your operator's APN before http_post().
Brown-outs during transmit are the usual cause of random resets: use a proper battery or a 2 A supply with a large capacitor.

pins.label: VBAT
pins.note: Li-ion cell or 4V supply that can deliver 2 A peaks

pins.label: PWRKEY
pins.note: Optional: lets maintain() power-cycle a hung modem (set_pwrkey)
